\iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.]

Content:
We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

Content:
[MATH: r_{u}^{′}|= ⟨(∂x)/(∂u), (∂y)/(∂u), (∂z)/(∂u)⟩; = ⟨(∂)/(∂u)(u), (∂)/(∂u)(v), (∂)/(∂u)(2v − 2u)⟩; = ⟨1, 0, − 2⟩; r_{v}^{′}|= ⟨(∂x)/(∂v), (∂y)/(∂v), (∂z)/(∂v)⟩; = ⟨(∂)/(∂v)(u), (∂)/(∂v)(v), (∂)/(∂v)(2v − 2u)⟩; = ⟨0, 1, 2⟩]

Content:
So, the fundamental vector product is

Content:

Content:
Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of [MATH: \mathbf{r}(u,v)] into [MATH: \mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}]

Content:

Content:
Then, we calculate the dot product of [MATH: \mathbf{F}] and [MATH: \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}]

Content:
[MATH: F(r(u, v)) ⋅ (r_{u}^{′} × r_{v}^{′})|= ⟨(u − v)^{2}, (u + v)^{2}, 12uv⟩ ⋅ ⟨2, − 2, 1⟩; = (u − v)^{2} ⋅ 2 + (u + v)^{2} ⋅ (− 2) + 12uv ⋅ 1; = 4uv.]

Content:
Therefore, the flux of [MATH: \mathbf F] through [MATH: S] is given by

Content:
[MATH: ∬_(S)⟨(x − y)^{2}, (x + y)^{2}, 12xy⟩ ⋅ dS|= ∬_(D)F(r(u, v)) ⋅ (r_{u}^{′} × r_{v}^{′})dA; = ∬_(D)4uvdA; = ∫_{0}^{1}∫_{0}^{1}4uvdvdu; = ∫_{0}^{1}2udu ⋅ ∫_{0}^{1}2vdv; = [u^{2}]_{0}^{1} ⋅ [v^{2}]_{0}^{1}; = (1^{2} − 0^{2}) ⋅ (1^{2} − 0^{2}); = 1.]

[MATH: \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{S} = \iint\limits_S \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n} \,\textrm{d}S = \iint\limits_D \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(u,v)) \cdot (\mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v) \,\textrm{d}A.]

Using the parametrization, where [MATH: x=u] and [MATH: y=v,] our surface can be parameterized as

[MATH: \mathbf{r}(u,v) = \left\langle u,\: v,\: -3u+2v \right\rangle]

over the domain

[MATH: D = \big\{ (u,v) \: : \: 0 \leq u \leq 2, \: 0 \leq v \leq 1 \big\}.]

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

[MATH: r_{u}^{′}|= ⟨(∂x)/(∂u), (∂y)/(∂u), (∂z)/(∂u)⟩; = ⟨(∂)/(∂u)(u), (∂)/(∂u)(v), (∂)/(∂u)(− 3u + 2v)⟩; = ⟨1, 0, − 3⟩; r_{v}^{′}|= ⟨(∂x)/(∂v), (∂y)/(∂v), (∂z)/(∂v)⟩; = ⟨(∂)/(∂v)(u), (∂)/(∂v)(v), (∂)/(∂v)(− 3u + 2v)⟩; = ⟨0, 1, 2⟩]

Now, the fundamental vector product is

[MATH: r_{u}^{′} × r_{v}^{′}|=|i|j|k; 1|0|− 3; 0|1|2|; = ⟨|0|− 3; 1|2|, −|1|− 3; 0|2|,|1|0; 0|1|⟩; = ⟨3, − 2, 1⟩.]

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of [MATH: \mathbf{r}(u,v)] into [MATH: \mathbf{F}(x,y,z){:}]

[MATH: F(r(u, v))|= ⟨z + 2y, 3y + z, x − z⟩|_{x = u, y = v, z = − 3u + 2v}; = ⟨(− 3u + 2v) + 2v, 3v + (− 3u + 2v), u − (− 3u + 2v)⟩; = ⟨ − 3u + 4v, − 3u + 5v, 4u − 2v⟩]

Then, we calculate the dot product of [MATH: \mathbf{F}] and [MATH: \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v{:}]

[MATH: F(r(u, v)) ⋅ (r_{u}^{′} × r_{v}^{′})|= ⟨ − 3u + 4v, − 3u + 5v, 4u − 2v⟩ ⋅ ⟨3, − 2, 1⟩; = (− 3u + 4v) ⋅ (3) + (− 3u + 5v) ⋅ (− 2) + (4u − 2v) ⋅ 1; = − 9u + 12v + 6u − 10v + 4u − 2v; = u]

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

[MATH: ∬_(S)⟨z + 2y, 3y + z, x − z⟩ ⋅ dS|= ∬_(D)F(r(u, v)) ⋅ (r_{u}^{′} × r_{v}^{′})dA; = ∬_(D)udA; = ∫_{0}^{2}∫_{0}^{1}udvdu.]

So, the missing expression is [MATH: {\color{blue}u}.]
